name: Colosseum Near-Real-Time RIC
what_it_is: A minimal O-RAN Software Community near-real-time RIC (Bronze release) adapted for the Colosseum wireless network emulator, providing E2 termination, E2 manager, routing manager, and Redis database as Docker containers. Part of the OpenRAN Gym project, it supports concurrent multi-base-station and multi-xApp connections with improved E2AP message encoding/decoding.
components: e2term — E2 termination container (handles SCTP connections from RAN nodes, port 36422)
e2mgr — E2 manager container (manages E2 node lifecycle, RMR port 3801/38010/4801)
sample-xapp — Sample xApp container connecting to SCOPE RAN via E2 termination
xapp-sm-connector — Service model connector performing ASN.1 encoding/decoding of E2AP messages
protocols: E2AP — E2 application protocol between RAN nodes and e2term
SCTP — Transport for E2 interface (e2term listens on port 36422)
RMR — RIC Message Router for inter-container messaging (routes keyed by message type IDs)
Redis (RESP) — In-memory state store between e2mgr and db on port 6379
measurement: RIC Indication Messages received from RAN node at 250 ms periodicity (default xApp subscription interval)
e2term container logs expose gNB connection events and message processing latency (nanosecond resolution shown in debug logs)
configuration: RIC_INTERFACE — network interface e2term binds to for SCTP (e.g., col0, can0, brric); passed as CLI arg to setup-ric.sh
RIC_SUBNET=10.0.2.0/24, RIC_IP=10.0.2.1 — Docker bridge network subnet defined in setup-lib.sh
router.txt — static RMR routing table mounted read-only into e2term and e2mgr containers; maps message type IDs to container IPs/ports
e2term_config.conf — mounted into e2term; sets nano port, loglevel, local-ip, sctp-port, trace mode, external-fqdn
GNB_ID — gNB identifier (format gnb:MCC-MNC-ID, e.g., gnb:311-048-01000501) injected into xApp at startup via sed
XAPP_ID — last octet of XAPP_IP used as xApp identifier for RMR routing
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection mechanisms documented; containers can be killed/restarted individually via docker kill/docker rm to simulate component failures
modes: Colosseum mode (default) — e2term exposes SCTP port via Docker NAT on the physical RIC_INTERFACE (e.g., col0)
Arena mode (--arena flag) — e2term runs without Docker NAT rules for co-located RIC and DU on the same machine (uses brric bridge interface)
constraints: Designed exclusively for Colosseum LXC container environment; base Docker images are only available to Colosseum users via the coloran-near-rt-ric-prebuilt container image
No docker-compose file — containers are orchestrated exclusively through shell scripts (setup-ric.sh, setup-sample-xapp.sh); no Kubernetes or Helm support at this layer
Static RMR routing table (router.txt) must be manually regenerated and containers restarted if xApp IP or message type assignments change
Single xApp IP slot pre-allocated (10.0.2.24); running multiple xApps requires modifying setup-lib.sh and regenerating routing table
Bronze release baseline — does not include A1 interface, O1 interface, or SDL (Shared Data Layer) federation present in later O-RAN SC releases
docker_services: db — Redis (dbaas:latest), IP 10.0.2.12, port 6379, network: ric
e2rtmansim — Routing manager simulator (e2rtmansim:latest), IP 10.0.2.15, network: ric
e2mgr — E2 manager (e2mgr:latest), IP 10.0.2.11, env: RIC_ID, DBAAS_PORT_6379_TCP_ADDR, mounts router.txt, network: ric
e2term — E2 termination (e2term:latest), IP 10.0.2.10, SCTP port 36422 published on RIC_INTERFACE, mounts router.txt + e2term_config.conf, network: ric
sample-xapp-24 — Sample xApp (sample-xapp:latest), IP 10.0.2.24, env: DBAAS_SERVICE_HOST/PORT, GNB_ID injected at runtime, network: ric
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml — container lifecycle managed entirely by shell scripts
No A1 interface or A1 mediator component
No AppMgr (xApp manager/onboarder) from standard O-RAN SC stack
No built-in metrics/monitoring stack (no Prometheus, Grafana, or VES collector)
No SDL (Shared Data Layer) cluster — single Redis instance only
No xApp descriptor or onboarding workflow — xApp is hardcoded and started via shell script
